DAHR and LOC identify the vocal roles and orchestra accompaniment, but not the orchestra’s name, conductor or acoustic substitutions. No individual instrumental timeline is asserted.

Acoustic recording of the named excerpt. Performing edition, cuts and studio instrumental substitutions are unestablished. No instrument-by-instrument timeline is supplied; the modern opera full score does not document this session.

The 17 March date and take 1 are documented by DAHR and LOC. Commons gives only the year 1907. The LOC transfer is a corroborating discographic source, not the streamed file.

Transfer
R. Wolfe — transfer credited by Commons; Adam Cuerden — slight hiss reduction attributed from Commons upload context Inferred, not documented

Commons explicitly credits the upstream transfer to R. Wolfe and documents slight hiss reduction. Adam Cuerden uploaded the altered file; his responsibility for the reduction is an attribution from that context rather than an independently named transfer engineer.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date established. The Commons, Archive and YouTube upload dates are not treated as digitisation or restoration dates.

[1]
Processing
Slight hiss reduction documented on Commons; parameters unestablished Documented

Only the described processing is documented; no equipment, filter settings, pitch correction or speed correction is inferred.

[1]
Composition rights
Underlying Puccini composition and historical libretto are public domain where ordinary life-plus-70 terms apply; no modern edition is claimed cleared. Documented

Commons marks the historical work public domain. This does not by itself establish the sound recording’s rights; the recording basis is separately documented below.

[1] [8]
Recording rights
Rule 2 — United States public domain: original sound recording issued as Victor 89006 in 1907, before 1923. Documented

DAHR’s original-issue MARC gives [1907]; Moses places Victor 89006 in the 1906–⁠1908 release group. Commons applies PD-US. The upstream Archive item is unavailable, so its original metadata and transfer licence cannot be independently inspected. No separate CC grant or worldwide clearance is asserted.

Giacomo Puccini, La bohème: O Mimì, tu più non torni. Enrico Caruso and Antonio Scotti, New York, 17 March 1907; C-4315-1. Internet Archive transfer credited to R. Wolfe, via Wikimedia Commons; slight hiss reduction in the Commons version uploaded by Adam Cuerden. Rights statement

  5. Internet Archive — linked R. Wolfe transfer (not opened) — Not opened: item page returned 404 and metadata endpoint could not retrieve item. No facts or numbers are cited from this unavailable source; R. Wolfe attribution is documented on Commons.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  6. Royal Opera House — La bohème, 3 October 2017 cinema programme — Page 2, Acts I and IV: first meeting, café departure, two men recalling absent lovers, friends’ meal and Mimì’s later return.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  7. Julian Morton Moses — American Celebrity Recordings 1900–⁠1925, UCSB Historical Discographies edition — Introduction explains that artist sections group records by release years, not session dates. Caruso: Victor Red Seal 1906–⁠1908 includes 89006 and 95200; 1909–⁠1911 includes 87043. Destinn: Victor Red Seal 1914–⁠1917 includes 88487. Opened as extracted text; not used to infer exact take or transfer pressing.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  8. Puccini Festival — Giacomo Puccini — Biography and work entries: early church work, Milan studies, librettists, source authors, premieres, composer’s death in 1924.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  9. U.S. Copyright Office — Classics Protection and Access Act — Term: recordings first published before 1923 ceased receiving the specified federal remedies after 31 December 2021. Sound-recording basis, distinct from composition copyright.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
